decision: Adopt symmetric capacity recovery B for both model arms; capacity triggers are mechanical and never performance gates.

supersedes_authority_revocation.reason: The user later approved one symmetric, reward-blind bounded capacity amendment after learning that both arms already used the same Agent System split algorithm.

text_memory_capacity_recovery.same_unit_repair_identity: the exact same 20 inputs in the same frozen order
text_memory_capacity_recovery.split_order: first 10 then last 10 in frozen order
text_memory_capacity_recovery.child_policy: each child gets one 2048-token primary and at most one exact-same-child 2048-token repair
text_memory_capacity_recovery.parent_policy: merge exactly the two child representations with one 2048-token primary and at most one exact-same-two-child 2048-token repair

agent_system_capacity_recovery.progress_guard: a split must reduce the node count; a single node never splits
agent_system_capacity_recovery.max_split_depth_basis: ceil(log2(unit_node_cap=20)); this makes the existing progress guard explicit without changing the accepted bisection path

skill_bundle_clean_replay.algorithm: existing full-20 hierarchical skill bundle path
skill_bundle_clean_replay.reason: No new Skill split authority is needed; the clean replay must demonstrate the already-observed no-split path.

seven_b_dormant_noop.interpretation: The later symmetric amendment is dormant/path-equivalent for 7B; history is not rewritten to claim the A2 fallback was used.
